Below are 30 conditional hypotheses covering the four gaps. Each is an interaction claim about an edit's effect on validation accuracy, and I expect the sign to hold across all three datasets.

**Parallel branches at summing nodes:** A conv added on one incoming edge should add less when a sibling incoming edge already carries a conv (redundant). It should add more when the sibling is none or pooling, because the conv is then the only learned path.

**Series chain:** A conv after a none predecessor has nothing to process, so it adds little. A conv after a skip predecessor sees an effectively shortened chain.

**Shortcut and compensation:** A strong direct edge 3 (skip) partially masks the value of edits elsewhere. When edge 3 is none, the other paths carry all the information, so edits there matter more.

**Self-replacement:** Replacing none with a conv yields larger gains than replacing skip or pool with a conv. The gain from a given edit is larger when the replaced op is weak (none).
